paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage. Moses sets a promise in front of Israel, and it is built on one small word: "if." He says, "if you faithfully obey the voice of the LORD your God," and then the blessings start rolling in (Deuteronomy 28:1). Notice who is doing the giving, though. Every blessing here says the LORD will do it, and Israel's part is to listen and follow.

So what does this teach you? God's commands are not a pile of hoops to jump through. Moses is describing a life lived under God's care, where the city, the country, the basket and even the kneading bowl are covered (Deuteronomy 28:3, 5). I think that's the whole point: God cares about the ordinary stuff, the daily stuff, the things you put your hand to. And when God's people live that way, Moses says all the peoples of the earth will see that they are called by the name of the LORD (Deuteronomy 28:10).

Now hear the last line, because it matters. Moses says, "Do not turn aside to the right or to the left from any of the words I command you today, and do not go after other gods to serve them" (Deuteronomy 28:14). Friend, the road is narrow, and the best thing you can do is keep your eyes on the One who is leading you. Keep walking with Him, keep listening, and keep your apron tied, because the teaching isn't over.
